findings.problem: The approved reading queue has documentation but no runnable implementation.
findings.principle: Implement the approved single-reader journey using the settled local Node/JSON stack and queue-owned state.
findings.consequence: A reader cannot yet save, find or mark an article read.
findings.fix: In a separately selected implementation change, build the smallest local application exposing save, list and mark-read through the queue; presentation uses those operations and JSON persistence remains behind that boundary. Exclude accounts, sharing and recommendations.
findings.verification: Run the actual local application against a disposable JSON file: save a title/address, find it, mark it read, then reopen the application and verify the same title/address and read state remain. Include read articles in the queue per glossary.md:4.

findings.problem: No executable check protects the approved first journey, and no project source defines evidence required to complete a change.
findings.principle: Proposed completion policy: affected approved journeys must pass on final inputs; unit tests alone do not establish the user outcome. Acceptance expectations come from the existing vision, design and glossary.
findings.consequence: Future implementation could pass isolated unit tests while persistence, article visibility or mark-read preservation is broken.
findings.fix: Alongside the first implementation, add one public journey check using real JSON persistence and restart/reopen; assert save/list/mark-read, preserved title/address/read status, and continued visibility of read articles. Add a short evidence section to DESIGN.md pointing to that check and its acceptance sources; expose one maintained native check command after its toolchain is selected.
findings.verification: The check passes the actual application with disposable storage and fails when marking read loses the title/address or when reopening loses saved state. Inspect expectations against VISION.md:5, DESIGN.md:3-6 and glossary.md:4-5. Record command, version, exit and output on final inputs.
